admission.justification: Without the line a refused Start looks as if nothing happened — the first sealed finding of the review round. The obligation is realized across the pane's state machine, the failure-line component and the four failure paths, and the review verified each path against its pre-change byte behavior.

applicability: Every ordinary failure of a control in the launcher bar: a refused or unresolved start, an unreachable host, a failed options or catalog read and a report that cannot be opened.
conditions: The line is the only text under the controls and is gone when the condition has ended or the next action of the bar has succeeded.
An unresolved launch is an actionable uncertainty, not a false agent failure; the line says what is unknown and what to do.
A refused dispatch stays visible through automatic reads; only an explicit successful action clears it.

A failed task-bound dispatch followed by a failed options read restores the base control behavior: the selectors and Start stay enabled and no Retry is offered by that path, while the one line still names the failure.
exclusions: The state line and reply text removed by rule 1 never return as a 'status' of the normal case.
Host-side frame notices (workspace, agent, availability) keep their own existing surfaces inside the frame.
A launch lock is a wait, not a refusal: it may show the actionable line and then clear when the reread answers.
